records.name: Philadelphia Zoo Volunteer Programs
records.summary: The Philadelphia Zoo recruits volunteers for its docent program, for special event shifts such as Boo at the Zoo, and for a teen program. Docents learn about the animals, then talk with guests at the exhibits and lead tours.
records.what_you_do: Docents train for about nine months, then give 50 service hours a year. Special event volunteers work shifts at zoo events and must complete one shift a year to stay active. Teen volunteers, ages 14 to 17, have their own program.

schedule.text: Docent training starts in April, July and January and runs about nine months. Special event shifts are posted by date, including Boo at the Zoo in October.

first_step.how: Apply through the zoo's online docent application, linked from its volunteer page, or sign up for a special events shift through the separate sign-up link.
first_step.basis: Docents need an application and about nine months of training before they work with guests. Special events shifts are a lighter first step.

records.notes: Same group as the existing record in research/done/w3-interests-b (philadelphiazoo.org/?p=1913). The importer should merge them by website. The volunteer page loaded directly this time, with no certificate error. Minimum age is 13, the lowest age on any listed program; the docent program requires 21. The page lists Volun-TEENS (ages 14 to 17) with no application link, only a note to email when the next recruitment opens. The page does not show a street address or a cost, so neither is recorded. Background check and interview steps appear in older pages but were not confirmed on the zoo's page, so they are not written here.

records.name: Wet Nose Rescue
records.summary: A foster-based rescue for dogs and puppies. Foster homes care for the animals until they are adopted, and the rescue also welcomes volunteers and holds public events such as a pet fair.
records.what_you_do: Foster a dog or puppy at home, sign up as a volunteer through the rescue's volunteer page, or come to a pet fair.

schedule.text: The adoption center is open by appointment only. Its pet fair is listed for a Saturday, October 10 (no year shown), from 10 am to 3 pm, at a Warminster park in Bucks County.

first_step.how: Fill in the foster application on the rescue's site, or start from its volunteer page under How To Help.
first_step.basis: Fostering starts with an application, and the site shows no walk-in time, so the way in is not open to drop-ins.

records.notes: The site lists a Northeast Philadelphia address (ZIP 19116) and a pet fair in Warminster, Bucks County. A search summary had called it a Southampton, PA rescue, so confirm the service area before treating Philadelphia as its home base. The volunteer page link on the site returned 404, so volunteer roles rest on the home page alone. The foster application page is linked from the site but was not opened. The pet fair shows no year, so the status is probably_active rather than active.

records.name: Forgotten Cats
records.summary: A trap, neuter and return group for homeless and feral cats, based in Delaware. It says it works across the Philadelphia region, and foster homes care for cats until they are adopted.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat or kitten (the average stay is about a month), help at the adoption center or warehouse, volunteer with fundraising, or help colony caretakers with trap-neuter-return.

first_step.how: Fill in the online foster application on the group's site. It asks about your home, your pet history, and three references.
first_step.basis: Fostering needs a written application and references before a cat is placed, so there is no walk-in way in.

records.notes: Service area conflicts across its own pages. The main page says it serves throughout the Philadelphia region, including Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland and Delaware. The foster page tagline says it cares for cats in Delaware. No Philadelphia address was found. Published at low confidence so the reviewer can decide. The newest dated item is 2025 annual statistics (no month given), so no last_sign_of_life is written. The footer copyright is not used as evidence. A 2021 WHYY article about Philadelphia foster recruitment listed it as a tri-state group seeking fosters.

records.name: Here Kitty Kitty Cat Rescue
records.summary: A foster-based rescue for homeless cats in Philadelphia. Cats live in volunteer foster homes, and adoptions use a foster-to-adopt agreement.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat in your home, or adopt one through the foster-to-adopt agreement.

first_step.how: Contact the rescue through the contact method on its WeRescue profile page and ask about fostering.
first_step.basis: The way in is unclear: the profile gives a contact email but no application form, visit time, or volunteer sign-up.

records.notes: No website of its own was found, so this record rests on one directory profile, which is the brief's low-confidence case for a group with no page of its own. The profile lists six cats available and shows no dates. Its contact email was obscured in our copy, so no contact is recorded. A search summary also said the group hopes to open a storefront rescue someday; that is unverified and not used.

records.name: PA Dog Rescue
records.summary: A Downingtown nonprofit that supports other dog rescues, mainly through online ways to take part.
records.notes: The site names only Downingtown, in Chester County, and does not mention Philadelphia. Ways to take part are online: an image quiz that donates kibble, an app to find adoptable dogs, and a form to promote a dog. The page lists no foster or volunteer roles. Named in a 2022 Philadelphia Citizen guide.

notes: Thin slice. The brief said to read done/w24-lists-thin/x-animals.json to skip recorded groups, but that file does not exist. I used inbox/w24-staged/x-animals.json (the earlier x-animals run, 11 records) and the animal files in done/w3-interests-b and done/w3-interests-e instead. Already recorded there and not repeated: PAWS, ACCT Philly, PSPCA, Morris Animal Refuge, Street Tails (STAR), Green Street Rescue, KittenSnatchers, PURR, Stray Cat Relief Fund, Schuylkill Center Wildlife Clinic, Philadelphia Metro Wildlife Center, Palmer Doggie Depot, Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia, CHOP pet therapy, Project MEOW, Comfort Caring Canines, Wagging Tails Brigade, Audubon Mid-Atlantic. The PAWS free pet food pantry, the PSPCA free pet pantry and ACCT's pet food pantry are programs of groups already recorded, so they were not added as separate records. Searches: three, all used (small rescues; zoo volunteering; pet food pantries). The youth-programs search was not run because the budget ran out. The only youth programs found are the zoo's Volun-TEENS (inside the zoo record) and Street Tails' junior volunteer program for ages 16 and 17 (already recorded), so youth coverage is still open. Mistake: I called mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context once by accident, which is not on the allowed list. It returned only a note that no widget had shared anything, and I made no other non-allowed calls. Access problems: FosterAPhillyPet returned HTTP 525 on two attempts; savedme.org has an expired certificate; arielsangels.org does not resolve; the Petfinder page returned 403; the Wet Nose volunteer page returned 404. No rate limiting was seen. Dropped with reasons: Providence Animal Center (Media, Delaware County, outside the city, not fetched); Emancipet (low-cost vet clinic, not a volunteer group); Doggie Style Pets (pet store); Le Cat Cafe and Fairmount Pet Shoppe (businesses); Sniffspot (directory aggregator); Philly Fur Foster (one person's Instagram account, not a group). Leads with no usable website (Super Moms, Canine Companions, All 4 Paws) are listed in leads_only.
